Oppermann, The molecular mechanism of nitrogen-containing bisphosphonates as antosteoporosis drugs, Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U.S.A. 103 (2006) 7829–7834. Reference [10]: J. Park, D. Rodionov, J.W. De Schutter, Y.S. Lin, Y.S. Tsantrizos, A.M. Berghuis, Crystallographic and thermodynamic characterization of phenylaminopyridine bisphosphonates binding to human farnesyl pyrophosphate synthase, PLoS One 12 (2017), e0186447. Reference [19]: J. Park, M. Zielinski, A. Mager, Y.S. Tsantrizos, A.M. Berghuis, Human farnesyl pyrophosphate synthase is allosterically inhibited by its own product, Nat. Commun. 8 (2017) 14132–14139.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - 2.7. Isothermal: Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) experiment [8,10,19] was carried out at 30°C with a MicroCal PEAQ-ITC system (Malvern, Worcestershire, UK). The purified FPPS and hits were prepared in the same buffer solution (50 mM Heps, pH 7.4, and 5 mM MgCl2) at the concentration of 20 μM and 300 μM, respectively. Each titration experiment was performed by a first injection (0.4 μL) followed by 18 injections of a hit solution (2 μL) into the sample cells (200 μL) with an interval of 150 s. The titration cell was stirred continuously at 750 rpm, and the initial delay time was set to 60 s. The titration data were corrected by subtracting the heat of dilution of hit into the buffer alone. The data were analyzed by the fitting model of “one set of sites” in MicroCal PEAQ-ITC Analysis Software.
original_paragraph.Results and Discussion - 3.2. FPPS inhib: Furthermore, the binding affinity of hits to FPPS was tested by isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) directly and the binding constant was listed in Table 1. The results showed that all the hits can bind with FPPS with Kd ranging from 14.3 ± 2.63 to 499 ± 18.2 μM, and VS-4 showed the highest binding affinity with the Kd of 14.3 ± 2.63 μM. Compared with the clinically used FPPS inhibitor ZOL, although the binding affinity of VS-4 was less than ZOL with the Kd value of 1.42 ± 0.170 μM, the inhibitory potency of VS-4 was encouraging for the discovery of novel FPPS inhibitors. In addition, hits VS-2, VS-8, and VS-10 had higher binding affinity to FPPS with the Kd value of 53.8 ± 1.85, 25.7 ± 2.91, and 48.1 ± 4.04 μM, respectively. The ITC results indicated that hits VS-2, VS-4, VS-8, and VS-10 might be potential candidates for FPPS inhibition. The correlation between theoretical binding affinity and experimental binding constant was analyzed. As a whole, the compound with a higher theoretical binding affinity showed a better binding constant Kd. Therefore, theoretical binding affinity prediction can be used for the inhibitory activity estimation and drug design or optimization.
original_paragraph.Table 1: The binding constant Kd/μM for VS-4 is 14.3 ± 2.63. The binding constant Kd/μM for VS-2 is 53.8 ± 1.85. The binding constant Kd/μM for VS-8 is 25.7 ± 2.91. The binding constant Kd/μM for VS-10 is 48.1 ± 4.04.
original_paragraph.Figure 3 caption: Fig. 3. Predicted binding modes of inhibitors VS-4 and VS-7 with FPPS. The superimposition of binding modes of inhibitors with FPPS, in which VS-4 and VS-7 were shown as green sticks (A and C) and the ligand in 4QPF was displayed as blue sticks. The key amino acid residues participated in the binding interaction with inhibitors (B and D). Inhibitors and the key residues were depicted as green and blue sticks, respectively. The green balls presented the metal ion Mg2+. Hydrogen bonds were shown as green lines, and the metal-mediated interactions between Mg2+ and residues were shown as yellow lines. (For interpretation of the references to color in this figure legend, the reader is referred to the Web version of this article.)

Oppermann, The molecular mechanism of nitrogen-containing bisphosphonates as antosteoporosis drugs, Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U.S.A. 103 (2006) 7829–7834. Reference [10]: J. Park, D. Rodionov, J.W. De Schutter, Y.S. Lin, Y.S. Tsantrizos, A.M. Berghuis, Crystallographic and thermodynamic characterization of phenylaminopyridine bisphosphonates binding to human farnesyl pyrophosphate synthase, PLoS One 12 (2017), e0186447. Reference [19]: J. Park, M. Zielinski, A. Mager, Y.S. Tsantrizos, A.M. Berghuis, Human farnesyl pyrophosphate synthase is allosterically inhibited by its own product, Nat. Commun. 8 (2017) 14132–14139.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - 2.7. Isothermal: Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) experiment [8,10,19] was carried out at 30°C with a MicroCal PEAQ-ITC system (Malvern, Worcestershire, UK). The purified FPPS and hits were prepared in the same buffer solution (50 mM Heps, pH 7.4, and 5 mM MgCl2) at the concentration of 20 μM and 300 μM, respectively. Each titration experiment was performed by a first injection (0.4 μL) followed by 18 injections of a hit solution (2 μL) into the sample cells (200 μL) with an interval of 150 s. The titration cell was stirred continuously at 750 rpm, and the initial delay time was set to 60 s. The titration data were corrected by subtracting the heat of dilution of hit into the buffer alone. The data were analyzed by the fitting model of “one set of sites” in MicroCal PEAQ-ITC Analysis Software.
original_paragraph.Results and Discussion - 3.2. FPPS inhib: Furthermore, the binding affinity of hits to FPPS was tested by isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) directly and the binding constant was listed in Table 1. The results showed that all the hits can bind with FPPS with Kd ranging from 14.3 ± 2.63 to 499 ± 18.2 μM, and VS-4 showed the highest binding affinity with the Kd of 14.3 ± 2.63 μM. Compared with the clinically used FPPS inhibitor ZOL, although the binding affinity of VS-4 was less than ZOL with the Kd value of 1.42 ± 0.170 μM, the inhibitory potency of VS-4 was encouraging for the discovery of novel FPPS inhibitors. In addition, hits VS-2, VS-8, and VS-10 had higher binding affinity to FPPS with the Kd value of 53.8 ± 1.85, 25.7 ± 2.91, and 48.1 ± 4.04 μM, respectively. The ITC results indicated that hits VS-2, VS-4, VS-8, and VS-10 might be potential candidates for FPPS inhibition. The correlation between theoretical binding affinity and experimental binding constant was analyzed. As a whole, the compound with a higher theoretical binding affinity showed a better binding constant Kd. Therefore, theoretical binding affinity prediction can be used for the inhibitory activity estimation and drug design or optimization.
original_paragraph.Table 1: The binding constant Kd/μM for VS-4 is 14.3 ± 2.63. The binding constant Kd/μM for VS-2 is 53.8 ± 1.85. The binding constant Kd/μM for VS-8 is 25.7 ± 2.91. The binding constant Kd/μM for VS-10 is 48.1 ± 4.04.
original_paragraph.Figure 3 caption: Fig. 3. Predicted binding modes of inhibitors VS-4 and VS-7 with FPPS. The superimposition of binding modes of inhibitors with FPPS, in which VS-4 and VS-7 were shown as green sticks (A and C) and the ligand in 4QPF was displayed as blue sticks. The key amino acid residues participated in the binding interaction with inhibitors (B and D). Inhibitors and the key residues were depicted as green and blue sticks, respectively. The green balls presented the metal ion Mg2+. Hydrogen bonds were shown as green lines, and the metal-mediated interactions between Mg2+ and residues were shown as yellow lines. (For interpretation of the references to color in this figure legend, the reader is referred to the Web version of this article.)
